sources.entry: Sonarr - Automatic TV Shows downloader and manager for Usenet and BitTorrent. It can grab, sort and rename new episodes and automatically upgrade the quality of files already downloaded when a better quality format becomes available. (Source Code) GPL-3.0 C#/Docker

summary.one_liner: Sonarr is a PVR (personal video recorder) that monitors RSS feeds for TV episodes from Usenet and BitTorrent, then grabs, sorts, and renames them.
summary.what_it_does: Sonarr monitors multiple RSS feeds for new episodes of followed TV shows and grabs, sorts, and renames them. It can scan an existing library and download missing episodes. It can also watch for better-quality versions of episodes already on disk and upgrade them automatically, for example from DVD to Blu-ray. If a download fails, it tries another release. A manual search lets the user pick any release or see why one was not grabbed automatically. The README also describes integration with SABnzbd, NZBGet, Kodi, and Plex (notification, library update, metadata), plus support for specials and multi-episode releases. It states support for Windows, Linux, macOS, and Raspberry Pi.
use_cases: Automatically download new episodes of TV shows
Fill in missing episodes in an existing TV library
Upgrade episode quality when a better release appears
Rename and sort TV files into a media library
Manage TV downloads from Usenet or BitTorrent
Feed a Plex or Kodi media library with new episodes
how_to_run: Download or install Sonarr from the project's Download/Installation instructions (linked from the README; exact commands are not in the README)
notable: Automatic quality upgrades for files already downloaded
Integrates with SABnzbd and NZBGet for Usenet
Notifications and library updates for Kodi and Plex
Manual search shows why a release was not auto-grabbed
caveats: GitHub Issues are reserved for bugs and feature requests only; support goes through forums, Discord, IRC, Reddit, or the wiki
README does not give install commands; setup is via linked installation docs
